utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Re, the Chamber has decided that you get the 15 minutes you said you'd still need. Mr. Tetaj, I'd like to remind you that the solemn declaration you gave yesterday at the beginning of your testimony still binds you. Please keep that in mind. Mr. Re, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning. To let the Trial Chamber and Defence know where I'm going from the consolidated of the 17th of April, these are the paragraphs which I will intend to lead -- elicit evidence, it's paragraphs 71, 86, 87, 88, 90, 91, 98, 100, and 106. It may be that at some point I may need to make an application under 92 ter if I can't get to it. Of course, I'm in the Trial Chamber's hands in relation to those particular paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tetaj. I want to take you to where we left off yesterday, and I'm going to ask you about a person called Astrit Berisha - that's paragraph 91 of the statement - who was a former member of Toger's unit. He was from Pozar. Now, did he tell you something about Toger's activities and members of his unit?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him. I know him. We met in Tirana. He told me that he was also from the war zone. He told me that only a very few soldiers had remained with Toger. He told me that the unit had been dissembled. This is what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, did he tell you anything about Toger killing members of his unit, who wanted to leave the unit?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He spoke to me, yes, but he wanted to justify his acts from the war zone, and exactly I remember what I told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your statement says that he told you that Toger killed every member of his unit that wanted to leave the unit in order to avoid them to talk about things that they had witnessed and actions they had taken part of. That's paragraph 91 of your consolidated statement of 17th of April this year. Is that what he told you?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you that we met in Tirana. We travelled in Tirana. He told me things. He tried to justify his departure from the war zone, the fact that he had left the area. This is what I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tetaj, I think we should make a clear distinction between what he told you and why he may have told you what he did tell you. So the first question put to you by Mr. Re is whether, as it reads in your statement, Astrit Berisha from the village of Pozar told you that Toger killed every member of his unit that wanted to leave the unit in order to avoid them to talk about things they had witnessed and actions they had taken part in. So the first question is whether he did tell you this. Whether true or not is another matter; for what reasons he might have told you, that's another matter. But, first of all, did he tell you what I just read as part of your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And did he tell you that he had escaped from Toger's unit in September 1998 because, according to him, Toger had already started eliminating his own soldiers because they knew too much, and he had been in Toger's unit from May 1998 until September 1998? And that's in your statement at paragraph 91.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you aware - and this is paragraph 71 of your statement - that Toger and his unit were involved in military actions in Prilep, Voksa, Carrabreg, and Loxha, when there were clashes between the KLA and the MUP, or VJ, between June and July 1998, and Toger never deployed his entire for an action unit but always selected three to five members of his unit?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did not go with the whole unit; that's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about the FARK, in paragraph 98 of your consolidated statement, in which you say that: "When FARK entered Kosovo from Albania around 22nd of June, 1998, they were stopped in Jasic by Ramush Haradinaj, Naim Maloku, and Sali Veseli for the following reasons: They were afraid that Tahir Zemaj would take over the command, they were afraid that the FARK would rule out the UCK/KLA, the FARK was known to be the official army of the Government of Kosovo in exile presided by Bujar Bukoshi and UCK he did not recognise the government as such." That's in paragraph 98 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see what happened. This was told to me by Tahir Zemaj. They told me that they went and they were stopped. There was a problem of that nature you described. I was not presented there. This is everything what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Tahir Zemaj tell you - this is paragraph 100 of your statement - that they were advised; that is, by Ramush Haradinaj and the other two, not to enter Kosovo and Tahir ignored that. And they proceeded anyway to Papracani, and you heard that there were some conflicts between the UCK and FARK?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you hear of two cases of FARK soldiers who were arrested and ill-treated by Ramush Haradinaj and his men in Gllogjan. That's paragraph 100 of your statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I am sorry that's a misquotation. Not two cases, one case of two people.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: One case of two FARK soldiers who were arrested and ill-treated by Ramush Haradinaj and his men in Gllogjan; one of them called Idriz Ukehaxhaj from Carrabreg.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about this. I was told by Tahir Zemaj in Prapaqan. That was an incident of that time. I did not know what happened further.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Idriz Ukehaxhaj tell you that he was heavily beaten and that they took 3.000 Deutschemarks from him, and were you told the second FARK soldier was from the village of Krusevac and he was shot in the leg?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard all about this in the barracks of Prapaqan, and there were other people who were present there, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Paragraph 106 of your statement, as far as you know, did Ramush Haradinaj convey his orders orally via messengers he sent or via work meetings he held on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Re, may I interrupt?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Are we in line with the original version? It seems to me that a paragraph is missing, at least in the numbering. In the English translation, paragraph 100 is following paragraph 98, and this seems to be the translation of paragraph 99, but I'm not -- yes, it seems to be because the 3.000 Deutschemarks are mentioned there. Without knowing enough Albanian, I -- you may repair that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The paragraph numbering is out. Paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It's just the paragraph numbering?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm reading the number which appears on page 28 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You're reading the English version paragraph numbering?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Not the Albanian version. It's a different numbering.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Okay. So there's no paragraph the 99 in the English version. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is but it is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Without text missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's not sequential. It seems to have been cut and pasted behind 106 -- sorry, 99 on page 28. I was going to 106 which is directly above 99 on page 28.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Yeah, on page 26 there is no para 99, so there it goes from 98 to 100.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: But then on 108, there is also a new para 100 after, 99 which is also appears on 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The passage I'm taking the witness to is numbered 106, and it's on page 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the question is: Did -- is it correct that as far as you know Ramush Haradinaj conveyed his orders orally via messengers he sent or via work meetings he held on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's paragraph 106, but that's not the paragraph 106 of the Albanian version. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's right, but the witness doesn't have the Albanian version with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So I'm reading the English to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, the Chamber would be pleased if we receive both languages, that at least the numbers are corresponding. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Tetaj.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through working meetings time and again. At that meeting, he gave us explanations and instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you leave the KLA in the Dukagjin area, together with Tahir Zemaj on the 8th and -- two FARK soldiers on the 8th of September, 1998, you leaving because you were suffering from a hernia and you needed proper medical treatment in Albania, and you agreed with Tahir Zemaj to withdraw from Kosovo to prevent civilian and military casualties since you were almost completely surrounded by Serb forces? That's paragraph 105 of your statement on page 28. And that you thought that this was a very professional decision that Mr. Tahir Zemaj had made?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The last thing I want to read to you is a passage, paragraphs 86, 87, and 88 of your statement, in relation to the kidnappings or disappearances of Serbs. I am just going to read it to you and ask you whether what's there is correct. Paragraph 86 says: "I do not know anything about the kidnappings or disappearances of Serbs in the Dukagjin area, with the exception of the cases of two Serbs called Milos, his last name is unknown, and Slobodan, his last name is unknown, from the village of Dasinovac in late April or the beginning of May 1998. I heard two different stories about the circumstances in which they appeared. The first that Deli Lekaj, the KLA commander in the village of Ljumbarda accompanied by his soldiers Haxh Lekaj, Zimer Ukaj, Sami Lekaj, and some others went to the village of Dasinovac. They were armed and dressed in KLA uniforms. They entered the house of Slobodan to loot it. They thought the house was empty since the Serbs were believed to have left the village of Dasinovac." Paragraph 87: "However, when they entered the house, they were shot at and Deli Lekaj got wounded. They returned fire during which allegedly the Serb called Slobodan got killed. Deli Lekaj was subsequently taken to the village of Pozar where he was treated by the local doctor, Syl Berisha. This is the story that Deli Lekaj told me afterwards. That is one version." " Paragraph 88: "The second version is that the above group headed by Deli Lekaj went to the house of Slobodan. The other Serb called Milos was at that very moment visiting his Albanian neighbour, whose name is Qaush Mehemetaj, brother of Halil Mehemetaj. However, when he saw Slobodan saw Deli Lekaj and his men coming to the house, he went to get Milos and told him to join him at his house. They both went back to Slobo's house. However, when Slobodan entered his house, he took his rifle and shot Deli Lekaj. He got wounded. As a result of this, the others apprehended Slobodan and took them to Gllogjan. They were taken to Ramush and Toger. "When Togeri heard that Slobodan had shot Deli Lekaj in the leg, he pulled his pistol and shot Slobodan in the leg as well. Ramush Haradinaj subsequently gave the order to take Milos and Slobodan back to the main road in Prilep where they could 'join their' forces, meaning Serb forces. The two were taken to Prilep where they were left behind; however, the KLA in Prilep being aware that the MUP and VJ would retaliate on them when they would notice that one Serb, Slobodan, was shot, took the two Serbs back to Dasinovac. "I heard people say that the bodies of Milos and Slobodan were found two days later in front of their houses in Dasinovac. I do not know who killed them. I heard people say that Lahi Brahimaj buried the two corpses in the vicinity of their houses next to the road, Dasinovac, Bardonic, Jablanica, because the local UCK had refused to do so." That's from paragraph 88 of your statement. All I'm asking you is this: Those are the two versions that are recorded in your statement. Are those the two versions you heard and told the Prosecutor about? And I emphasise heard, not saw.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is all hearsay. This is what was said at that time. Everything is hearsay. Prosecutor insisted that I should say what I had heard, but I've not seen anything. The Serbs in Decane, even before Gllogjan was attacked, during the first attacks in Decane, all the houses were abandoned. The Serbs had left the houses. Very rarely you could see any family there. Probably in Rasic there was one were two. It was an old couple there who I visited. But the different versions are versions which I heard, not what I have seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just on the fact that you'd heard them, the version which involved Ramush and Togeri, can you remember now who you heard that one from?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were the variance which was said at the time, but I don't know anything accurate. I don't remember who told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you for the extra time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tetaj, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Emmerson, as I take it from the fact that you are on your feet, Mr. Emmerson. Mr. Emmerson is Counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, just before I begin cross-examination, two things, if I may. First of all, there are some documentary bundles to be circulated; one for the witness and the appropriate number for the Court and the interpreters and the Prosecution and so forth. I wonder if that might be done now so we can save time in the course of cross-examination. The index indicates where the particular document has already been marked for identification. There are two points just to alert Your Honours to. On the 21st of June meeting, Your Honour yesterday mentioned the fact that the provisional translation had failed to reflect across the manuscript annotation of date and place. There is, in fact, an official translation which is in the bundle as well, in the bundle that Your Honours is going to be seeing, although it has a different ERN number, but it's the same document with the passage missing that Your Honour referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that, Mr. Re, you will find a way of getting the official translation as - what is it? - P140 in the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then the other point to make is that I have put into the bundle both versions of the 23rd of June minutes; that is to say, the original rough version in original Albanian and translation and the typed version. So they're both there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's P141 and P142.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. That's the first collection of matters. The second, and it arises out of the examination this morning, and it may just for the sake of caution be a precaution if the witness would just very briefly remove his headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tetaj, could you remove your headphones for a second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Re asked certain questions about paragraph 100 of the consolidated witness statement and the incident about which the witness had heard concerning Idriz Ukehaxhaj. It will certainly save me some time in cross-examination if it can be established as common ground that that is the incident about which we have already heard oral testimony through the evidence of Witness 7/29, Witness 29. And it's clear, transcript 3505, line 1 in the evidence of Witness 29, that that is the same incident that's being described.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, could you please check that and assist Mr. Emmerson in saving time - of course, if you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We needn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have got the line there, because usually searching through the system goes quicker if you have one or two words.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, Idriz Ukehaxhaj is one way of looking for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But it is 3505, line 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. I take it that you'll get a response by Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll have a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It needn't delay matters at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can the witness put his earphones on?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tetaj, I want to start, if I may, by asking you some questions about the 24th of March, 1998, that is the day that the MUP attacked the Haradinaj family compound in the village of Gllogjan. This is something that you've mentioned in your witness statements but didn't -- weren't asked questions about by Mr. Re. First of all, prior to that incident on the 24th of March, had you heard, yourself, about the MUP attacks in Drenica at the end of February and the beginning of March on the Ahmeti and Jashari family compounds in Likoshan and Prekaze? Had you heard about those?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you: What, from your observations, what effect did the news of those two attacks in Drenica have on the Albanian civilian population in the area where you were living?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It caused a great panic because they were attacked. There was an operation from the Serb police forces. The communication was attacked. It was a very unenviable situation for the population at the time and for the villages, including the village where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were people in the area around where you lived, were they aware of the extent of the killing that had happened in those two incidents, the number of people killed?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. They knew because everything came across from Drenica because the events were mirrored by the radio and television of Pristina. And all the corpses of the Jashari family were seen by all the people across Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In your consolidated witness statement - and whenever I refer to a paragraph of your witness statement, unless I indicate otherwise, I'm referring to the consolidated longer statement that was made in April - at paragraph 12 of that statement, you say that you could hear the sounds of the MUP attack on Gllogjan on the 24th of March from Donja Luka. You personally could hear it?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've heard myself and I saw it myself because in aerial distance it was very short. It's a 6-, 7-kilometres long distance. It was mid-day so I personally saw it and heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can you describe from where you were what you could hear and see, please.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During the attacks on the Haradinaj family in Gllogjan, there were many helicopters involved in the attack. They attacked. They fired rockets and heavy firing was heard. From inside the village you could see smoke, billows of smoke, and I was curious to see what was going on at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just be absolutely clear, did you see rockets being shot from the helicopters?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I saw them personally with my own eyes. You could -- if he got on the upper floor, you could see everything because the weather was clear, the sky was clear, and you could see everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, at paragraph 15 of your statement, you say that two or three days after the event you went to Gllogjan, in effect, I think to see the reality of what had happened there. Can I ask you this: Can you describe for us what it was that you saw when you got there. There's a reference in your statement to a lot of material damage caused by the impact of the air-strikes. Can you just give the Trial Chamber an impression of the extent of the damage.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Two or three days later after the Serb forces had withdrawn, I decided to go in person to Gllogjan. In Gllogjan, in the centre of the village, at the Haradinaj and around the Haradinaj family compound, there were many houses destroyed. There were many people arrested by the Serb police forces. On the road, I saw bombs and grenades, M-57 of the Serbian army, and some of them were unexploded, so we marked them. And as far as I remember, an officer of experience, Daut Haxhe, it was his field of specialty, he came to dispose of these unexploded ordnance. So we tried to tell the people to avoid walking on the unexploded ordnance which were left behind which hadn't been exploded, and they were from the Serb forces. There were many ruined houses. It was a silence, a dead silence, people were in panic, very few people around. There was an old man there, who was some 90 years old, and I met him. I can't remember his name. He couldn't move. He was handicapped and he was very old, and I went to see him. So the situation was very, very serious and unenviable.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you refer to the unexploded ordnance, and you've described it as the M-57 of the Serbian army, I just want to be clear, are you suggesting that this ordnance was identifiable as VJ ordnance or could it have been MUP ordnance?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both the army and the MUP used the same ammunition because the colour of the grenade or the hand-grenade or the bomb, judging from the colour, they were used both by the MUP and the Yugoslav Army. So both of them used the same ammunition; and by the initials that the ammunition carried in the Serbian language, we knew that they were used by both. So I cannot say that they were either of MUP or the VJ because they were of the same colour. It was the same ammunition used by both.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand. I understand. Thank you for that clarification. Did you also on that occasion learn of the three teenagers who'd been killed on that day?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had heard about it. Some -- some of them were fleeing from the violence. The site where it had happened, it was far from the village. They were fleeing the fighting, and I attended their funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the information that you've just given us about the circumstances in which they died, is that something you learned from other people?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During the funeral, I heard people talk about how they were killed, yes. They were -- there were speeches at the funeral, and they talked about the moment when they were injured and killed. That was at the funeral where I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Apart from the fear and panic you've described, would it be fair to say there was some anger amongst the villagers about what had happened?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was anger, not only from the people in the very place where the killings had happened, but all across the region. People were angry because they did not know what would happen to them the next day. Nobody knew what methods they were going to use, and fresh attacks were expected. There was a great panic and anger, and that was because people were not organised and they were unprotected. They didn't have a home to go back to. They didn't know what the next day would bring, and this was being discussed among the villagers. Everybody had their own versions of the story. But from my experience I know it was a tragic day, not only for the Haradinaj family who defended -- resisted the attack on their house and they defended the village. And they tried to defend everyone. It was a critical moment for all the region, not only for the Haradinaj family.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you told us yesterday that after that incident, there was a process by which you began to organise people within your own village into a village defence in the first phase after the 24th of March, and I want to ask you some more questions about that aspect of your evidence.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, in your witness statement, paragraph 40, you say that you were the only person in Donja Luka with a uniform. Can I just ask you, first of all: When did you first get your uniform?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the moment that we started to receive weapons, the weapons came from the person who I mentioned yesterday, and he brought me only a jacket, military jacket. It was about two months after the event that I got hold of this jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And how long did you remain as the only person in Donja Luka with a jacket or a uniform?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose, in my village, I was the first and the last person to have one. The whole of the rest of the village was civilian. Those people who managed to buy a weapon for themselves, they had it, but all the rest of the village were civilians. I was the only person in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Are you saying that remained the position until you yourself left Kosovo in September?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about the village, my village?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Are you saying -- sorry, let me put the question to you --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my village, from the moment I left. Yes, yes, continue with -- yes. From the moment that I left Kosovo with the soldiers of the FARK, I was the only man in uniform in my village.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you also described in your statement - and you mentioned it in your evidence yesterday - how some of the other villages close to Gllogjan had started to form their own village guards. And you mentioned particularly in your statement the villages of Dubrava, Baballoq, Gramaqel, Shaptej, and Lumbardh. That's paragraph 22.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very briefly, if you will, can you just explain to the Trial Chamber from your own knowledge or what you learnt at the time, how those village guards came into existence. What was the process by which farmers, people with ordinary day-to-day jobs, what was the process by which they formed village guards?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each and every village, as I said, in their own way made preparations because of the fear they had. So there was this self-initiative from every village to do something, to take the precautions, because the same thing could happen in their own village. So they got together, a group of people, to decide what they could do for the future. They decided to send the village guard to find out who was coming in and out of the village, and I did that in my village and it happened in the villages surrounding ours, and that is how the whole thing expended. But please remember that they were not soldiers. They were ordinary people. They were people who was 60, 70 years old. So there were people who were younger, of course, but I could not call them soldiers. They were volunteers. They wanted to defend their village, their house, and the surroundings with all they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Up until this point, before the 24th of March, was it typical in those villages for there to be a village leader, a mayor, somebody who was regarded by the village as a person who would be turned to if village matters needed to be decided? Was that a typical structure of village life?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a fact that in the villages there were political party structures in several villages. The party leaders, the leader of the democratic party, was a person of authority and people referred to him; and according to the Kosovo tradition, it was normal to listen and to get the advice from this person of authority. That's true. There was a person in each and every village who had led the village in a way. And this was even without the -- that was prior to the organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. But, for example, in your village, who would that person have been?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my village, there was Halil Tetaj, Sami Gecaj. They were representatives of the democratic party. From the moment Gllogjan was attacked and we started to get the guard, village guard organisation, then I was being trusted with that because I was a military officer. I had been imprisoned for five years by the Serbs. So after that, in my village, people were relying on me; and in other villages, they would come from other villages to consult with me what to do in those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just briefly, if you would, two questions: First of all, did the village leaders, as far as you could see --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did the village leaders, as far as you could see, play any role in this self-initiated organisation of the villages that you've described?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were representatives of that group.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just to be clear, when you went to that meeting that you've told us about at the end of May that Ramush Haradinaj had issued an invitation for, were many of the people --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- were many of the people who attended there the village leaders from civilian times?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. All those people of authority in their own villages, they were there because not every village had people of military experience like myself. So those present there were elderly people or civilians who had led the village life for ages. And more than 80 per cent of those present were in civilian clothes. And they didn't have any weapons at all because they don't know where to get them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you've told us about - and you've mentioned in your statement - a particular cluster of villages in the area around Gllogjan, but is it right to say that a similar pattern was occurring further afield, for example, in Isniq where Skender Rexhahmetaj came from, that there was the same process taking place up there?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The same happened in other villages, but there were villages, smaller villages, with fewer households. There were villages that were sparsely inhabited, but the organisational structure was similar in all the villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In your testimony, yesterday, you described your first visit to Gllogjan in April when you went to speak to the commander who turned out to be Ramush Haradinaj. Can you help us just in any more detail about the date of that visit?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember the exact date, but it was after -- after the attack on the Haradinaj compound, two, three weeks after that. I can't remember exactly what date. It was two, three, or more weeks after that. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So is it fair to say sometime around or after the middle of April?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's somewhere -- yeah, sometime then. It could have been a month after the attack, maybe. I'm not sure, but I'm sure it's around about that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In your statement, when you described this meeting - this is paragraph 35 - you say this, and I'm just going to read you a short sentence or two. You say that Mr. Haradinaj told you that: "I should organise my village on a village level. He said that later on they would establish UCK HQs in every village, and then they would call the representatives of each village HQ to form a Joint Command." First of all, did he give you, as far as you can recall, any impression as to how long he thought it might be before it would be possible to call people together in that way?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't remember this, but I remember that he invited us for a consultation and he informed all the villages that the situation was very serious and complicated. And he asked for the opinion of all people to express their opinion on their villages. Nobody could predict how things would move on, so it was just a consultation that we had. So it was just -- he was one of those people who were trying to keep things going, to keep people up-to-date with what was going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I draw your attention to page 21, line 7, you said you would quote, and since the consolidated statement is not in evidence, the real quote should have been: "I should organise my village in a military way on a village level."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just a moment ago, Mr. Tetaj, you said that he invited us for a consultation. Is that the invitation that was sent out on the 25th of May that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you now turn to tab 1 at the bundle, because I'm just going to work through some of these documents with you?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn to tab 1 in the bundle, and I'm going to work with you, if I may, briefly through the bundle. Some of them you've already seen and some of them you haven't. Tab 1 has the original Albanian and English translation of the invitation that you received dated the 25th of May for a meeting on the 26th of May, and it's marked for identification P123, P123. Can I ask you this: Between the first time you went to Gllogjan and met Ramush Haradinaj and the meeting on the 26th, Mr. Tetaj, had you been to Gllogjan in the interval, or was this the first time you went there after your initial visit?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the first visit, this was the second one. I've not been any more time in between these two visits.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So for a period of a month or more, you had no contact with Gllogjan between your first visit and this visit. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, could you please make sure that having no contact is the same as not going.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I entirely take the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've told us that in that month you didn't visit, yourself. Was there any communication passing between yourself and Mr. Haradinaj during that month before you received this or not?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I think the interpreter might not have got the whole of your answer. Would you repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this was the first contacts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even there, would this mean that there was no communication through telephone or in writing or through a courier who would send a message? Was there no communication at all during that month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was the initial stage. So I had the first meeting and then I met him for the second time; but during the period between these two meetings, I have had no communication with him. There was also no reason for him or for me to contact him. I was -- so, at that time, I organised the people who went to get the weapons. So during the period you are talking about, there was no contact and there was no reason for me to contact him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said at the time you organised the people who went to get the weapons. Was there no communication about how to get the weapons with --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were the people who went out to get the weapons, and then they came back during -- I had no contacts with the people when -- after they left. I met them when they returned. During that period, I had no contacts with Ramush either. During that time [indiscernible] the first round of weapons and ammunitions. So until the first stage when we began our organisations, we had no contacts with him, with Ramush.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And was Ramush involved in how to get the weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. He was in Gllogjan. We were in contacts with Albania at that time. We sent the people across the border. It was very, very risky. These people took the courage and they went there, so it was through the contacts we had with Albania at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, at the meeting on the 26th of May, is it right that it was you who proposed the creation of the four subzones that you marked for us on the map yesterday, that was your suggestion?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think you said yesterday that after that meeting, so 26th of May onwards, from that point you considered yourself to be a part of the KLA. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of the other people who were there at the meeting on the 26th of May, was it your impression from what you could see and what you knew of them that these were people who were already within the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The majority of the representatives were, as I said, they came there with the hope. They knew that something was happening, that UCK was emerging. The morale was stronger. People were more optimistic, despite the risks we faced.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, the first combat --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I see Judge Hoepfel has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Was your question answered sufficiently?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I regard that as a sufficient answer; but if Your Honour would like a supplementary question asked, I'm perfectly happy to ask one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I move on then to the very first combat you were involved with because you told us about this briefly yesterday. But the first serious combat that you became involved with took place just two days after that meeting, is that right, on the 28th of May?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness use the two microphones, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think one of your microphones has gone off. Just bear with me a moment.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you told us a little bit about that yesterday, but I just want, if I may, to try to clarify some of the details with you. In your consolidated witness statement, paragraph 62, you indicated that the MUP and the VJ had approached Vranoc from the direction of Peje with tanks, armoured vehicles, and heavy weapons. First of all, can I ask you just to be clear. Are you certain that the VJ was involved in that operation as well as the MUP, or could it have been the MUP alone?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: A part of them had tanks, that part belonged to the Serbian army; however, the overwhelming forces wore police uniforms. This is what I saw with my own eyes. The tanks were army tanks. They did not have blue colour. They were not tanks belonging to the police; they were tanks typical of the Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just give us an impression briefly, if you will, of how the Serb forces conducted that operation in Vranoc. What did they actually do?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The early hours of the morning the column left from Peje barracks. It passed through Vranoc river. They came together. They took position against the villages of Streoc and Dubrava and Kryshec and Dubovik, and then they came to the cross near Vranoc. It was a construction project there, a kind of building which was being constructed. They placed their heavy artillery of the army there. The infantry and the police forces then attacked from the other sides of the hill of Vranoc. So then they used the hill of Vranoc as a kind of position, and then they carried out this operation during the whole day. They opened fire with the tanks against the houses in Vranoc, in lower Vranoc, in upper Vranoc. They also destroyed the mosque and the house of the person who served in the mosque. They were tanks of the Serbian fire which opened fire. This operation continued until 6.00 in the afternoon. The village had some organised civilian forces, but they were very, very small. They had very few weapons. They tried to resist. Our houses are of stone and we took position in these houses, and we opened fire from there against the enemy. I also took part. I was on the other side of Lumbardh, and I took position in lower Vranoc. I had people with me who were volunteers who had come with me. They were all civilians. They had light weapons and they took position with me. I gave them orders. I was there personally. I gave them orders through my mouth. I also tried to use some people to convey my order. That was very, very difficult because it was fire coming from all directions, from the Serbian police. We had only light weapons, and we had -- we were also subjected to shelling from the artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You mentioned in your witness statement, para 62, that on their retreat the Serb forces attacked Dubovik and Krusevac, and that similar actions took place the same day in Streoc, in Isniq, in Carrabreg, in Rastavica, and in Prilep. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. After the withdrawal, at 6.00 the Serbian forces went into a column. They withdrew, I saw them, then they went to the direction of Dubovik and Kryshec, as well as to the road linking the area with Peje. They went to the village of Dubovik. They opened fire time and again. They stopped a little longer at Dubovik, then they went to Streoc. They didn't go from Vranoc but from another road from the river of Vranoc; and then they mounted other attacks, then they went to the direction of Decane. At the bridge of Dem which links Decane, they mounted this uninterrupted attacks against the village of Isniq. There, Avni Poduxhaj was killed. He was killed Lumbarda. He was killed on the same day. Then in Carrabreg they made similar attacks. They went to the direction of Gjakove; then they stopped at Prilep and they opened fire again on Prilep. During the way -- during their movement, they opened fire. It was sporadic fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you this: Was there also an attack that day on Vranoc?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vranoc was still not in the system of the organisation we had; therefore, Vranoc was left aside. I don't remember any attack on Vranoc. .

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And a village called Lybeniq, do you know Lybeniq, was there an attack there?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. During the way from Raushic on the right side, if you come from direction of Decane, is the village of Lybeniq. They opened fire against that village, too, and they did the same thing on Strellc as I described to you earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Lybeniq and Streoc are quite close to the main road, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lybeniq, if you go from direction of Decane is on the right side of the road; Strellc is on the left side. They are -- they are probably about four kilometres between each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, the British military attache to Belgrade visited those villages in the days immediately following this incident and was informed that forces answering the description of the JSO had killed 11 villagers in those villages in this attack. Can I ask you: Were you aware of the civilian casualties in Lybeniq and Streoc or, indeed, military casualties? Were you aware of the number of people who had been killed in those two villages?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were five people killed in Lybeniq. There were some other people in Strellc killed. I don't know their names. In Isniq I told you that there was one person killed. There were dead people, yes, but I don't remember exactly the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, finally, on the detail of that offensive, we've heard evidence in this Tribunal from a police officer who was shot at on the 28th of May driving along the road very close to Lybeniq and Streoc and who was shot and hurt in the leg. Can you tell us the young soldiers or KLA volunteers who would have been deployed in that area, under whose overall subzone would they have come?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Streoc was in subzone number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that would be --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember about any officer. What officer are you talking about, Albanian or Serbian officer?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. A Serbian MUP officer who was shot and injured in the leg by a group of young -- it was an incident that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. I only know that this area belonged to subzone number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That would be under Skender Rexhahmetaj and Gani Gjukaj?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, Skender Rexhahmetaj and Gani Gjukaj. Rexhahmetaj and Gani Gjukaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, leaving aside the attacks in Drenica and the attack on Gllogjan on the 24th of March, was this the first concerted major Serbian offensive in the region?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Decane area and Gllogjan, in Prekaze, however, also in Likoshan, in Laushe, we saw on television that there were attacks on these areas I just mentioned. There were attacks from MUP and paramilitary forces in other areas of Drenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When were they? Sorry. When are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me about the moment when Gllogjan and Haradinaj family was attacked, so you asked me about attacks from that moment, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let me put my question to you again, and I'll do it slowly because it may be that it wasn't clearly enough phrased: Leaving the attacks in Prekaze and Likoshan and the attack on the Haradinaj compound, leaving those to one side for a moment, this assault on the 28th/29th of May, was that the first major Serbian military offensive attacking a number of villages in the Dukagjini area?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The village of Prilep was attacked earlier, the Carrabreg village was also attacked earlier, Slavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the villages around Gllogjan, they were attacked, even before.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to move to looking at the map that you marked for us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't know at what point it would be most convenient to take our break. I'm happy to do it now if that's the most convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It depends if you can deal with the map in some five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's do it now and then have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to come back in a little while to look in more detail at the minutes of the meeting that took place in Jablanica on the 23rd of June; but, first of all, we can see from the zones that you've marked on this map that as at the end of May, they did not any area to the west of the main road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And they obviously did not include Jablanica either?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the moment when the original staff of Dukagjin was set up, Jablanica was a separate zone so it was not included in these four subzones. It was not included in them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that was what I wanted to ask you. You say until the -- the translation reads the original staff of Dukagjin was set up. Can I just be clear. Are you saying until the meeting on the 23rd of June when the staff of the Dukagjini Plain was established, until then, Jablanica was not part of this coordinated grouping. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And neither was Junik or Reka e Keqe?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These areas were not included there. We had these four subzones. The other ones you had mentioned were not included in them. There were Serbian forces. Carrabreg was not there. The line that is the areas which are divided by Carrabreg, they were included, so Jablanica, Junik, Carrabreg, all of them were not part of the subzones.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But there were, obviously, were there not, KLA groupings, clusters, in those areas?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, can you just help us with this. After the 23rd of June meeting, after the staff of the Dukagjini Plain was set up, could you indicate for us on the map the other areas which joined together to become part of the Dukagjini Plain operational zone. First of all, you mentioned Jablanica. Can you give us an idea of the area around Jablanica that you would be referring to on the map; and if necessary, perhaps you might mark it with a different colour, a green or a red.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I've seen that the map has now been -- the marked map has now been uploaded. Would you like to make the witness the markings on the electronic version or the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think on the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- on the hard copy. Is that a spare copy that has been provided to the witness, or is it the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's the original. If Your Honour would rather they be marked on the screen, they can be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, we have assigned an exhibit number to the copy of this document as marked by --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's easiest to do it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Either he should be provided with another colour copy or the marking should be done --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think it would be helpful to have them in conjunction with one another rather than on two separate documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we could use the one on the screen, perhaps, you could take the pen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber prefers to have the marking be made on the screen, so on the electronic copy. But perhaps then we first, Mr. Emmerson, if you would -- is this the size you'd like to have it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is fine, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's first ask whether the witness is -- could I, Mr. Tetaj, we will work from the screen at this moment. Are you able -- perhaps with the assistance of the usher --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- are you able to find your way on the map on the screen as it is now? Is it clear enough for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Before you mark it, can I ask you this: When the meeting on the 23rd of June occurred and the staff of the Dukagjini Plain was established, was Jablanica in a zone? Did it have a zone or was it merely the town of Jablanica? How did it work? Was there an area around Jablanica that was regarded as the zone or not?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was just the village. It was the village of Jablanica until then.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And after the 23rd of June, can you indicate for us which areas became a part of the Dukagjini Operational Zone, which centres of KLA activity?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the creation of the regional staff of the Dukagjini plateau, the subzones that I mentioned yesterday, they have been marked here. They were part of the operational zone of the Dukagjini plateau. Jablanica, Kosuric, Junik, Vranoc, and the road leading to Loxhe, Rausic, on the western side Junik, Smolice, Jasic, and other villages in the area. This region was called the Operational Zone of the Dukagjin plateau. There was no subzones 1, 2, 3, but it was called the Operational Zone of the Dukagjin plateau.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So did the original four subzones continue to exist after that, or did they cease to exist as separate subzones?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As names, as numbers, all these subzones were functioning as they originally were; but in reality the people who used to lead these subzones, they were given new assignments. They had new duties under the new organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. With that explanation, I'm not going to ask you to make a particular marking. And since you haven't made a marking --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we zoom-in on zone 1 for a moment. And once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, there's one matter of clarification I want to seek from you about the deployment of Serb forces that you've indicated here.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, you drew a distinction yesterday between Baballoq and the hill which is near Baballoq, and I just want to draw your attention to two features. If you look immediately to the left, that is to the west of Gramaqel, you can see --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gramaqel, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to the west, just to the west of Gramaqeli is an elevated area called Erecka Suka. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pause there for a moment. Just to the east of Gramaqel, above the words "D. Bites," Donji Bites, there is Radonjicka Suka. --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Donji Bites.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Immediately above that, yes.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Suke of Radoniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. There were two elevated sections there, two elevated hills in other words. I want to suggest to you that there were Serb forces stationed on both of them. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were there and I have seen them with my own eyes, and they were shelling the Haradinaj compound from there. I was at a height where I could see shells 102-millimetre artillery firing, and they were targeting the village of Gllogjan. They were stationed in this area, and they were on the Suke of Baballoq. They opened fire on Gramaqel from there. The village of Baballoq lower down was on our side, controlled by us; but the heights were controlled by the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear, Serb forces on both of those two hills?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. The Suke of Baballoq was right from the start in their control, and it was a big problem for us because they had taken control of these heights, key points, and they were very close to the residential areas and our forces as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And may I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask one second. Mr. Re, we heard evidence of a similar nature in the past. Is there any dispute about Serb forces or Serb artillery on these elevations, apart from what they exactly did, but it has not been pursued by Mr. Emmerson in great detail on when or how the Haradinaj compound was shelled from one of these positions. But is there any dispute about the presence of artillery units on these elevations?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The area in which there may be dispute is the time when they were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we should focus on the time and then anything else. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I can conclude this in just a couple of minutes, and I'll come back to that question in just one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tetaj, can you see to the east side of Lake Radoniq another hill called Suka Cermjan? Do you see that, Suka Cermjan, it's just to the east side, the right-hand side of Lake Radoniq?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Were there Serb artillery forces stationed there as well?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Suke of Cermjan, that was called the door-step, as it were, because it was used for aerial attacks. It was used by the anti-aircraft artillery, and all the guns there were aiming at Zhabel and Grgoc. I was there when they fired from there, when they fired their artillery from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you now on this map, please, draw a circle around those three hills; Erecka Suka, Suk Radonjic, and Suka Cermjan and hatch them in the way that you have the area of Bitesh, so that we have it clear the areas that you have marked as --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please. We first have to zoom.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, and I think one more time. One more in. Could we zoom-in just one more. Thank you. And it might be convenient to mark them in blue so they don't get confused with either the red or the black.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a blue?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, please, all three of them. You can mark them with a cross or a circle. It's entirely up to you.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also, in Prilep, there was a hill where the Serb forces were stationed, and that's on the opposite side. If you look at the road between Gjakove and Decane, there was a hill by the road where the Serb forces were stationed, the police forces; and from that hill, they could see the area around Junik, and they had fired from there towards Junik and Prilep.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you first mark Suka Cermjan for us, as you've described, and then mark the hill you've just described near Prilep.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I've marked these 1, 2, 3, and then I'll do the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, there seems to be some confusion. Mr. Tetaj, the third marking you made is on the north-western side of Lake Radonjic, which on my map reads to be Slatina. That's not, as far as I understand, what Mr. Emmerson had in mind when he was referring to Suka Cermjan. Could you please try to find Suka Cermjan, or were you actually thinking of Slatina when questions were put to you in relation to Suka Cermjan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought it's right here, but I'm not clear about this map. Now I'm looking at it now. I'm sorry. I've made a mistake. I am sorry. The Suka Cermjan is right here; it's 699, the number on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Now, just to be clear, in the centre, you've got two blue circles, one above the other. Is the top circle, is that a mistake? Because if there's one of those circles that is an error, would you please put a across through it now.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to make an improvement on a mistake which I made yesterday. I'm looking at the black line. Maznik was part of subzone 3, the village of Maznik.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, my attention was drawn to the possibility of erasing a marking if someone would like.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, perhaps, in order to avoid further confusion, I suggest that with the assistance of Madam Usher that the Slatina marking will be erased.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now we see on the screen that it is erased.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need a black pointer. The colour of this pen is blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I have a black pointer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you for a second. You're asking for a black pointer in order to include to include Maznik in subzone 3; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The village of Maznik which I made a mistake yesterday, I wanted to improve that with the black pointer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this moment, we can't do that because this one has been stored and has been assigned; but if there's any correction to be made, it seems that Mr. Emmerson is not extremely --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm happy with the fact that we that have on transcript and it's clear from the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Finally this, because we have to take a break in just a second, Mr. Tetaj, but whilst we still have the map in front of us, I want to ask you about the period of time that there was Serb forces stationed on these three hills. First of all, was there Serb forces stationed on those hills from the 24th of March onwards?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the start of the bombing on the Haradinaj compound, the Serb forces for the first time came with their military units, and they settled there in the forest of chestnuts, which wasn't mentioned here; and then they occupied the Suke of Bitesh and that of Baballoq. They were stationed in these points. Later on they took the Suke of Cermjan. So with time, these three positions, they had been there for a while, the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As far as you are aware, can you tell us did they remain in those three elevated positions throughout the summer and into September when you left?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the contrary, they brought on reinforcements.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And on the two hills to the west of the lake, Erecka Suka and Suka Radonjic, was the shelling to Gllogjan from both of them or from one of them?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shelling of Gllogjan was carried out from the forest of chestnuts with artillery, but most of the shelling took place from Bitesh. So Gllogjan was attacked from Bitesh mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Finally this, when you say "the forest of chestnuts," can you indicate to us, is that a place you've already marked?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I haven't marked it because we didn't talk about it. I cannot see it on the map, on this section of the map. It should go further down so that we can see that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. We can't move it at this stage.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was close to the Decane monastery. Before the Serb forces moved to the areas we talked about, they were stationed near the Decane monastery.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And finally this, was the shelling of Gllogjan something that took place intermittently but consistently right the way through from April to September?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From April to September, yes, frequent shelling. The artillery shells of the Serb army, they fell on the meadows of Prekolluku and Irzniq. There were positions set up there, and the electricity circuit which was supplying electricity to the area was damaged from the forest of chestnuts because the distance from that place to Gramaqel is about 13 kilometres. The artillery that they were using was able to shell these areas --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- these villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And thank Your Honour for the extension of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because the five minutes have now become 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Do you want us to save that screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, if that can be marked for identification and tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, the number for this now again marked but now with blue markings map would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be exhibit D38, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Tetaj, we'll have a break and we'll resume at 20 minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I mention two matters briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Re has kindly confirmed that the confirmation I sought at the outset of my cross-examination that the two incidents referred to in respect of Idriz Ukehaxhaj are the same; in other words, it is the incident from which we've heard evidence from Witness 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Secondly this: Just on the question of timing for today, with Your Honours' permission, my intention would be to conclude by the end of today; in other words, by quarter to 2.00. Is that the acceptable to the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This also depends on how much time the other Defence counsel would need. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. I believe I'm going to need about an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: About an hour. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It will be very short, if there's anything at all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In view of the fact that the Prosecution has taken effective three hours and 55 minutes, I think it would be fair that you conclude by today and that other Defence counsel would conclude in the first session tomorrow morning. We'll then in the second session tomorrow morning deal with some procedural matters and then most likely not a third session tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want, if I may now, Mr. Tetaj, to take you to some of the documents, the minutes of various meetings. I'm going to try to ask you short questions, and I'm going to try to invite you to give me short answers so that we can move reasonably swiftly through them. Can we start, please, behind tab 3 with the minutes of the meeting of the 21st of June, which, as the minutes record, took place in Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For Your Honours, both translations are behind that document, the unofficial and the official translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There were three aspects of this minute I want to ask you about, Mr. Tetaj. First of all, we can see from the list of those present that in addition to Mr. Haradinaj, Shemsedin, which is presumably Mr. Rexhepaj. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's how I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And we see a little further down Skender Rexhahmetaj, who was the, you've told us, the joint subzone commander for zone 4. In addition at that meeting, were Lahi Maxhupi and Nazmi, were they Lahi and Nazmi Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The object of this meeting, putting it shortly, was to discuss coordination. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this document yesterday for the first time. I confirmed that the meeting took place. I was present there; however, I have never seen Nazmi and Lahi Brahimaj being present there together.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how their names have been included here. This is not even logical to have Nazmi and Lahi, both of them present at the meeting. Lahi is written here, but it was -- he was not written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I think if we look down the minutes --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Halim Tolaj, and this is another name which I don't remember seeing there at the meeting. I don't know him personally; however, I also don't remember him being present at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Well, it may be that your recollection is playing tricks on you, Mr. Tetaj, because there are various comments in the minutes themselves that are recorded as having been made, I think, by one of the Brahimaj brothers, by Maxhupi, that is Lahi Brahimaj, but we'll come to that in a moment or two. First of all, if you will, if you look on your copy; that is to, say the Albanian version, just about halfway down the page, and on our copy that's --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I say something? Dauti was not there. Ramush was there, but Daut was not there. Rrustem was not there, too. So Daut was not there. I remember there very well. Daut, and not Nazmija, and Lahija Ramush, they were never together. I'm talking about only those meetings at which I was present myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, just listen carefully and look at the minutes, if you will, with me for a moment or two. This is a meeting that took place just two days before the 23rd of June meeting in Jablanica, and it's plain, I would suggest, from the very opening lines of it that the purpose of the meeting, as the text says under Mr. Haradinaj's name, is: "Coordination of common activities. So far we can say that it was the Dukagjini headquarters." That's the opening remarks of Mr. Haradinaj; and he goes on to say: "Reka, Dushkaja, i.e., Jablanica, and Gllogjan should be included here. At any given moment, the subzone with the most urgent need should be assisted and the forces should be sent from the Dukagjin HQ." Do you see those opening words?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, now you are quoting from the draft translation. Wouldn't it not be better to, since I take it that the official translation will replace the draft translation, that you quote from the official one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You're quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Let me put it on to the record: On the official translation, the opening words are: "The reason for the meeting is to coordinate joint activities at Dukagjin level. So far we can say that there has been a self-proclaimed Dukagjin staff to some extent. This ought to include Reka, Junicko Polje, Dushkaja, i.e., Jablanica, and Gllogjan.
