At the given moment, we need to assist the subzone which has the greatest need and forces should be sent from the Dukagjin staff." Now, just pausing there, Mr. Tetaj, and if you look halfway down the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And for Your Honours, it will be towards the bottom of page 1 of the official translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You are recorded as saying this: "We have taken a step. We are in favour of cooperation. For those zones that we have, we should work in coordination with Jablanica. We are in favour of joining up with all the representatives of those zones. We are happy for all activities to be coordinated, for us to share tasks." So that is recorded as your contribution to the meeting, Mr. Tetaj. Does that reflect your thinking at the time?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you could now look, please, for me at the contribution from Ramush Haradinaj that follows. There's your contribution, then there's a contribution from Maxhupi and from you again and from Maxhupi, and there then follows a contribution from Mr. Haradinaj. So the last full paragraph on your first page. Does that begin with Mr. Haradinaj saying that: "The purpose of the activity" --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does it begin with him saying: "The purpose of the activity is to get everyone together in a single family like one working body"? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: All right. Now, I now want to --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I now want to look with you, if I may, about halfway down that body of text, and I'm going to start reading the English translation. So it's halfway down the large paragraph on page 2 in the official translation from Mr. Haradinaj's contribution. The subject is: "Advancing the work, specifically the Kosovo Liberation Army must be transformed into a superbly organised army, a superbly directed functional and well-regulated army without any splits, parallelisms, dark sides, gangsters, vandals, and without any serious vices, fratricide, et cetera. This method closes the way to rumour-mongers. Wherever you go, it has be the same. It will not depend on him, not on me, not an Ali, not on anyone individual. We meet once a week. Having one sole body will have its own advantages. If it seems too early to you, we can leave it until another time; however, responsibility for any inactivity will fall upon us."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. Too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then just a little further down, just one sentence further on it continues: "We have still been unable to work in the Dukagjin Zones that have not yet been liberated. Things are progressing in general. Should anyone be able to do something, let him do it. In critical situations, I may perhaps have a possibility of helping someone, but I may not know where they are in the field in order to help them, what to take with me, and where to deploy. We do not know what the situation is in Celopek, Vranoc, et cetera."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And he goes on: "If it is not necessary to know all this, then okay" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He says: "If it is not necessary to know all this, then okay; but in the opposite case, it would not be reasonable. We need to make efforts to get out to you today and to the towns." Pausing there, Mr. Tetaj, is that your recollection of the position on the ground, that there was a lack of coordination and communication that this series of meetings was trying to address?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. This was a working meeting. We discussed all these issues which you just mentioned. We also discussed about how we could take a further step so that in the next -- at the next meeting these three areas would be included. Before that meeting, we discussed the transformation of the staff into the regional staff. We had problems with coordination and we discussed this. The idea was to improve things, to set up a structure, to have coordination like a proper army has coordination. So it's true that we discussed all these issues. I had some problems with the names of the people who I remember they were not there. It's a long time ago, so probably I'm not right about their presence; however, I remember that at those meetings Nazmija and Lahija were not present. Lahija was there but Nazmija not. Again, I ask for your forgiveness for some --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Don't worry about that, Mr. Tetaj, but can I ask you, again, just try to remember to keep your answers a little shorter and a little more focused on the specific questions, just so we can get through the material we have to cover. If you look at the third line up from the very bottom of the minutes, so if you look to the very end of the minutes, the last line on the second page, if you look to the third line up from the bottom, I think it's clear, is it not, that the meeting ends with Mr. Haradinaj indicating that there's only going to be one issue to decide at the next meeting, and that is organisational personnel planning. The very end of the -- if you look -- I think you're looking in the wrong place, Mr. Tetaj. If you look at the very bottom of that page,, three lines up from the bottom, there even an entry: "Ramushi." Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ramushi at the next meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And is it clear from that that the only item to be decided at the following meeting on the 23rd would be reorganisation?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This had to do with the organisational system.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if you just look a little further up on that page, there's a heading: "Regarding the military police." And if I can just summarize it very briefly, it looks from the minutes as though two different -- it looks from the minutes as though two different draft suggestions have been discussed about the possibility of establishing a military police in the Dukagjin region. And about halfway down the third main paragraph, Mr. Haradinaj is recorded as saying: "The item which talks about the responsibility of the information service, we are still not at such a level of organisation as to have an information service here." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you, please, to confirm that as at this period - that is to say, the end of June - there was no military police organisation in the Dukagjini region?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Until that moment, until those meetings, there was no such structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we could just go slightly out of chronological order, briefly, and turn to tab 24 at the back of the bundle, there is a minute there of a meeting of the 25th of July which you are recorded as having attended, although it looks as though you arrived late. Do you see that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but just a moment. Yes, I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you're first listed as absent, and then at the very end of the attendees it says: "Rrustem Tetaj arrived in the meantime." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just at the very top, just above the first line that runs across the page is the list of people who attended. First of all, you're listed as being absent and then it says: "Rrustem Tetaj arrived in the meantime." Is that right? Mr. Tetaj, just here.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. "Rrustem Tetaj," yes, but I can't read it properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to read. Yes, yes. Yes, you are right. "Arrived in the meantime," I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, immediately under that line, there is a recorded contribution from Mr. Haradinaj - just bear with me a moment - after the first line in, the second line it goes on: "Work on the creation of the military police. The police to be organised into platoons and with commanders and deputy commanders for the area, for example, the Reka area, one platoon, et cetera, eight platoon commanders constitute one leading command." And then this: "We have thought of Tigri as commander of the police, and the General Staff has approved this. The brigades support the idea of a military police," and so on. Now, pausing there for a moment, Tigri is a man called Fadil Nimonaj. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fadil Nimonaj, yes. Tigri was Fadil Nimonaj, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you've told us a moment ago that there was no military police in existence as at the 21st of June. Is it also the position, therefore, from this minute, that there was no military police in existence, as at the 25th of July; although, efforts were being made to try and create one?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I want to go to the meeting of the 23rd of June, which is behind tab 4 and tab 5. Can I just explain this to you briefly, Mr. Tetaj. You were shown yesterday -- behind tab 4. You were shown yesterday some minutes of the meeting at Jablanica on the 23rd of June, and they were the handwritten minutes that were obviously taken in the course of the meeting itself. There is a second set of minutes, which are typed up behind tab 5. So you've got two sets of minutes of the same meeting, one is behind tab 4. I think you're still behind tab 3 there. Perhaps if the usher could just help you. Behind tab 4 is the document you looked at yesterday.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then behind tab 5 is a typed version slightly different wording but essentially the same information. Just a few questions on these minutes with you, if I may. I'm going to use the typed version because it's slightly easier to follow, except for in one respect. First of all, can I ask you to look, please, in the Albanian of the typed version. So behind tab 5 look at the second page, just turn over on to the next page. Yes. About halfway down, do you see Tetaj, your name, there?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So this is your contribution in the 23rd of June meeting; and again, if I can just summarize it briefly, I think you are in support of the idea of coordination. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At the bottom of that paragraph, you refer to a military school which is ready. Was that the military school in Prapaqan that you were then referring to?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll come back to the Prapaqan school in a little while. And if you just look to the next entry against your name, which is just halfway down the following page, so the opposite page, it was you, I think, who proposed Mr. Haradinaj as commander of the new Dukagjin Plain Operational Zone. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, finally, with these minutes, could I ask you just to turn back to tab 4 now, to the handwritten minutes, and find the very last page.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as I was informed by Haradinaj, after I came here, I didn't know anything about Smajl. Rrustemi was not there, but I can see here the name of Smajl here. So I'm not very much clear, I am confused.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can look at it in the original.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to Ramush Haradinaj when you mention Smajl?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we can actually look at the original minutes as they were written. If you turn back to tab 4. All right. Can you turn back to tab 4, yes? And if you find -- if you look at the numbers in the top right-hand corner of the pages, do you see it? In the top right-hand corner of the page, there is a number, Mr. Tetaj. If you look at page 3, it's on the right-hand side of the document you are looking at, at the moment.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look at the bottom of that page, page 3 --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- it recorded: "R.I. Tetaj proposes R. Haradinaj." Do you see?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that how you remembered it?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you just turn two pages further on. Right at the end of the minutes there is a list, which does not appear in the typed minutes, of titles given to people at this meeting. Obviously, we know that Ramush Haradinaj had been elected commander, and you told us that Lahi Brahimaj had been elected deputy commander and Sali Veseli Chief of Staff. Now, I just want to ask you one or two questions about that list, if I may, for a moment.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see it. It's printed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We have that in relation to this at the last few lines of page 5 of the English translation and on to page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tetaj, you told us yesterday on a number of occasions that some of the titles that were used in the developmental phase of the KLA in the Dukagjin region, titles like "HQ" and "commander," were what you described as big names which didn't reflect the reality.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does that also apply to some of these posts that are listed here, that comment?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That's correct. These are the names we wanted to use in order to make progress, in order to have good morals, to make progress. The idea was good; however, there is difference between theory and practice. It was -- we are talking about that particular moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's what I wanted to ask you about. Skender Rexhahmetaj, so the joint commander of subzone 4, has made a statement to the Prosecution in this case in March 2006. And referring to this list at paragraph 42 of his statement, he says this: "Some of these appointments never actually came into effect, for instance, mine. This was because we never actually got the anti-tank equipment." Now, we can see that -- we can see that Skender Rexhahmetaj is listed as anti-armoured combat unit. I mean, did that title mean anything in real terms, Mr. Tetaj?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is said was correct. I was deputy -- deputy Chief of Staff. I was in charge of logistics. Of course, these are big titles. But if you don't have the arsenal of weapons, if you don't have good supplies, then this means that the titles are good on paper, but they are, indeed, a bit bloated, let's put it this way. So what you said was quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, just to be clear, in relation to Skender Rexhahmetaj, can you confirm that what I just put to you is correct; namely, that his appointment was effectively meaningless because there wasn't any anti-tank equipment available for him to command?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was fictitious. We thought that time would come when we would have that. We were just preparing for that time to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And talking of bloated titles, somebody called Muhamet Berisha is appointed as head of biological and chemical defence. What did you understand that might mean within the emerging KLA village structure?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember who this person was. I'm not sure whether I've seen him before. I see the name now on the paper; however, if you want me to respond more specifically, this is a fictitious title. We're talking about perspective here. It had nothing to do with biological and chemical means at that time. We had nothing of that sort at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I mean, the reality is these were grand-sounding titles which were aspirational. They were to make you sound like you were an army.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In reality -- I'm sorry to say this, but in reality, I also said yesterday we use a lot of word like "headquarters," "commander." These are titles, unfortunately. I do not want to lower the value of what KLA did because we started from scratch. The ideas were good; however, the use of these names was fictitious for that particular moment. I don't know whether you understand me.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I understand you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I do not know whether the Chamber is greatly assisted by generalising. I mean, if there are no biological and chemical defence units, that, of course, does not allow for the conclusion that everything on that list is -- for example, if I see assistant for sabotage combat, Toger, then in some sweeping statements everything's out, which might not reflect the level of accuracy and precision we would need.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Does Your Honour wish me to go through the list one by one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But at the same time it's not that difficult with the example of biological and chemical defence to say all the titles were nonsense. It's the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. But Your Honour has the other answer as well; namely, Skender Rexhahmetaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I may say so, the thrust of what I was seeking to elicit is that these documents can't be taken literally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That we cannot rely on -- okay. The point has been clearly made, and I take it you also understood my message.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we turn to tab 6, please, which is the minutes of a meeting that took place the next day at which you were present, as was Ramush Haradinaj. And I just want to ask you one or two questions about that, first of all. We can see -- and this is for you, it's about -- do you have that document, tab 6? Yes?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 000352. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's the one. That is obviously a meeting of the 24th of June. You're recorded as being present, as is Sali Veseli, Lahi Brahimaj, and Ramush Haradinaj, and others.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, if we look towards just about below halfway down in the Albanian and a little further down on page 1 of the English translation, we can see the Chief of Staff; that is to say, Sali Veseli, setting out a training plan, and that follows on with a number of bullet points over the next page and a half, a fairly detailed form of training plan. Can I ask you this: Was that a training plan that was going to be put into effect at the Prapaqan training centre that you were establishing?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's the idea. The idea was that in Prapaqan village where we had the barrack, to have brief weekly training.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The Prapaqan barracks were already then available for use by the KLA in that area, were they?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. When I went there, it was already organised. Our idea is that -- was that people who had no skills to use weapons, to undergo some brief training so that they could become more familiar with light weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's important just to deal with the Prapaqan barracks, because of the questions you've been asked about the relationship between FARK and the KLA, which I'll come on to in just a moment. If we could look halfway down the third page. So once the bullet points are over, the following page, there is a discussion about 20 tons of flour which had arrived as emergency aid in Isniq and five tons of it has gone missing, and there was a discussion about the possibility that people were misusing resources. And there is then a record of a comment made by Sali Veseli in which it is suggested that a communique should be issued on misuse of resources. And just at the end of that paragraph - so in your copy it is just over two-thirds of the way down the page - there is a sentence which reads: "For every propaganda against the KLA in my AOR, measures will be taken before the military court."

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There wasn't, in fact, a military court in existence at this time, was there?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Absolutely, there was no such court.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, again, just for the Trial Chamber's understanding of these kinds of documents, why would it record that action would be taken in a military court if there wasn't one?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was done in order to address the public, in order to raise the morale. We wanted to tell people that we are in the course of setting up such things in order to prevent bad things from happening, you know, bad things which might happen. So this was a communique in order to inform the public about the military court, but there was no such military court. The conditions were not ripe for such a court yet. However, this was an idea, to set it in the future if things proceeded well. This was simply on paper. There was nothing concrete.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So no military police in operation in the Dukagjini area, no military court, but message is being sent out -- is it fair to say message is being sent out to create the impression that you were a functioning army amongst the population?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct. We wanted to create a better image.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we just look a little further down towards the bottom of that page, the very last group of entries in the minutes, we can see that money is handed out by Ramush to a number of you; Skender Rexhahmetaj, yourself, Shemsedin Cekaj. So it is only zone commanders, and an additional sum to you and Sali Veseli. Was this money being handed to you for the purposes of furnishing and equipping the Prapaqan training centre?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was money for the subzone. There were shortages of flour and elementary things. This was the money we could use for those purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You appear to have been given an additional sum over and above the sum that was given to the other subzone commanders, and the question I'm putting to is: Were you given that money at that meeting to assist in equipping the Prapaqan training centre?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for furnishing the training centre in Prapaqan, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, obviously, just so that we can put these dates in context, this meeting took place on the very day that FARK forces first arrived in Junik, is that correct, 24th of June?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Junik, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Or at least in --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't know that they were on the way, so we didn't know -- we did not have any information about them coming. We proceeded our course. We planned to hold this activity, and that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you more questions about the FARK relationship in just a second, but turn behind tab 7 if you will.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The reason, Your Honours, you will see behind tab 7 multiple copies of the same order. It is simply because that's the way the exhibit arrived. So rather than pack it about, there's many, many copies of the same order in Albanian, but it is only one order. The English translation is obviously there only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tetaj, this is an order to you dated either the 8th or the 6th of July, because it says 8th of July in type form and then the words -- the number 6 --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and then the number 6 is written in manuscript across the top. Now, this is an order from Ramush Haradinaj to you, specifically, as well as being copied to Naim Maloku and Driton Zenelit. Putting it shortly, is this an order asking you to open the Prapaqan barracks, which would be called the Jusuf Gervalla Centre, and appointing you the chief of the centre?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This was an order for me. I was appointed as chief of Jusuf Gervalla Centre in Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then we can see that at item number 5, commanders of various units are asked to appoint their most distinguished soldiers with military training to assist in the realisation of the education process. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see. That is how it was. The idea was to set up the centre and other units to send people on a weekly basis so that these people could undergo such course. They should have -- they should learn how to use the weapons. So all the people in charge were asked to assist in this process.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then if we turn behind tab 8, there's a list of KLA soldiers who are assigned by Ramush Haradinaj on the same day to the Jusuf Gervalla Centre. Is that correct? Do you see his signature at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct, yes. Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now, pausing there, it follows from what you've told us, that the Prapaqan barracks were operational by the 8th of July with a training centre run and funded by the KLA; correct?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now I want to move on to the FARK issue with you because by the 9th of July, and certainly by the 10th of July, FARK officers had been allocated to the Prapaqan training centre, hadn't they?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. The arrival of Tahir Zemaj with 22 officers and several soldiers - I can't remember the exact number - they came from Jasic and they came to Prapaqan, and they were for there and we organised for them to settle in the Prapaqan barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: First of all, I think they stayed in some houses in Isniq, and then they were welcomed by the KLA under Ramush Haradinaj's authority. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I was the one who admitted them. I welcomed them, together with Skender Rexhahmetaj and several other.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to ask you about Skender Rexhahmetaj because in the witness statement he's made for the Prosecution, paragraphs 22 and 23, he says that the soldiers who came in with Tahir Zemaj included 84 soldiers that he had sent from his subzone; in other words, that they were KLA soldiers that had come from subzone 4 across the border to join up with Tahir Zemaj, and then had come back over with them. Now, is that right? Were there, in fact, people from the subzones who'd gone over the border to become part of the FARK unit that came over?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel kindly slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's true, especially from the area of Irzniq, where Skender Rexhahmetaj was in control and part of them joined the soldiers from FARK.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Your Honour was going to raise an issue with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're referring to the statement. Where do we find that statement so we can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can get a copy for Your Honour. I'm simply putting the proposition to him at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand, but the Chamber would appreciate to get a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The proposition, though, is right that there were soldiers coming from subzone 4 over the border to join with Tahir Zemaj's men and come in under his control. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The soldiers who were with Tahir Zemaj, they came from across the border; but the other soldiers, that came from subzone number 4, they joined the soldiers that came across from Albania. They did not go across to Albania, but they joined the FARK soldiers when they arrived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. So that is at the beginning of July. Is it the 8th or 9th of July?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So this is now a blended force of officers from the fourth subzone of the Dukagjini Staff who have blended in at your barracks under the command of Tahir Zemaj?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's correct. We were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, in terms of the dispute between Ramush Haradinaj, on the one hand, and Tahir Zemaj on the other, is it right that there was a difference of opinion between them, which centred on whether the military-trained officers who had come in with FARK should be dispersed to the villages who had been fighting on the front lines?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look. Both on the part of Ramush and myself, we noticed that Tahir Zemaj had come to the barracks of Prapaqan, and he -- he had found everything that was available there. Tahir Zemaj, as a commander of FARK, with all the soldiers, they mixed up with the soldiers from the KLA. And up until the moment that he left on the 8th of September, there was nothing that was achieved from him. It was Ramush Haradinaj who tried to coordinate things at -- with the meeting in Prapaqan.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand. But what I'm trying to be clear about with you, just that you can make the position clear, if you will, to the Trial Chamber. Is it correct that the essence of the disagreement between them was about whether the trained officers that Zemaj brought in with him should stay together and try to fight a conventional military war or disperse among the villages within the existing structure of what was essentially a guerilla force. Was that the difference of opinion?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tahir Zemaj had the idea that we form operational brigades; and when the Serbs attacked they can intervene, the brigades, and then come back to base. But at that time that was impossible. So in the Dukagjin area, there were very few career military officers. There were many volunteers who were holding makeshift positions. And my opinion, as well as Ramush and others, believed that we should distribute the trained officers around at various points, rather than have them at a computer base in Prapaqan. But we would rather have them on the ground, on the front line, where the proper defence was taking place. And this was a normal diversity of views. There was disagreements between Tahir and Ramush and myself, and many things evolved in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just be clear, Prapaqan was the only proper barracks in the whole of the area, was it not? It was your best facility?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the only centre. It was a makeshift centre in the form of a school where we could do whatever we did. If you set up a form in a school in another village, a similar one, the villagers feared that the village would be attacked by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The simple proposition that I'm putting to you, Mr. Tetaj, is that Ramush Haradinaj allowed Tahir Zemaj to occupy the best training facility that you had available in any one of the four subzones that you had. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you've described the nature of --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've described the nature of the disagreement, and Mr. Re this morning took you to two particular incidents that were referred to in your witness statement; one, an incident in which a man called Idriz Ukehaxhaj had been injured. You were told about that.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Idriz Ukehaxhaj, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the second incident that's referred to in your witness statement is an incident where Ramush Haradinaj turned up at the Prapaqan centre and got very angry with the officers of FARK --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and expelled them from the Prapaqan centre for 24 hours before allowing them back. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, first of all, can I ask you this: Apart from those two incidents, to your knowledge, was there ever any other incident of conflict; that is to say, violence between FARK officers and the KLA? Was there ever any other fight between the two, apart from the two incidents that you've described?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was only these two incidents, and the first incident I didn't see myself but I heard it being referred to Tahir. And in the second one, I was there, both together with Ramush. And we were there when Ramush spoke and I spoke. They left the barracks because they admitted that they were not implementing the rules there at that moment, at that time. Later on we agreed to rejoin, and I was the middleman, as it were, at another meeting where we agreed to have them back.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, in your witness statement, you suggest that that incident at the barracks, the second of these two incidents where Ramush excluded the FARK officers for 24 hours, you suggest that that happened sometime in August. I'm going to suggest to you that your recollection of that is wrong, and that it happened on the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about it. I apologise if I'm not accurate with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's not a memory test. I'm going to clarify the date with you in a moment, if I may. But just to be clear about this. After that incident occurred, first of all, Ramush spoke to the soldiers that were in the Prapaqan barracks, and they were perfectly welcome to remain. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You then spoke to the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Yes, yes. I was there and I spoke after the speech by Ramush, and I said something after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, in effect, was your message to the soldiers, "Look. We'll sort these misunderstandings out?" In effect, was your message to the soldiers that, "We would sort these misunderstandings out?"

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And later that same day, did you then bring the two sides together at a meeting in Lluka?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And was it all resolved that afternoon at the meeting in Lluka?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you could just look behind tab 10 for a moment, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think we need to go into closed session, if we may, for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The request that you've just been looking at behind tab 11, so that's P192, does that reflect a blending then under one command structure of the commanders of the command as it was with the commanders of FARK?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the record, Mr. Emmerson, it would be P193.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least on your list, but you also provided us with a new list without any further explanation. I see that 11 there suddenly is P192. So we'll now replace the old index by the new one.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I think there was an error, simply a typographical error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there any other change in it or is this the only one?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The only other additions, Your Honour, at items 12 and 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We have indicated the English translation references.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which are not in the original document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just for clarity then the correct reference is P192 for this list.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I put the question to you again. Does that request by Tahir Zemaj represent a blending between the commanders of -- who had come in with him under the banner of FARK and the commanders of the subzones who were already operating in the KLA structure?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if you could just look behind, very quickly, behind tabs 12 to 17. If you could just flick through those briefly to familiarise yourself with them. They work in pairs. Each of them is an authorisation followed by an order, both of which are signed by Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You're supposed to read the numbers of --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of the MFI in the transcript, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. So they will be P197 for tab 12; P199 for tab 13; 65 ter number 25 for tab 14, which will require to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It says also P194 in the new index.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm corrected. It has been marked for identification. It's P194.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's one of those documents that appears twice with different ERN numbers, so that is the confusion. Tab 14 is P194; tab 15 is P200; tab16, P198; and tab 17, P201.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to summarize, these are authorisations and orders dated the 11 and 12 of July, appointing the three brigades, which had then been blended. Is that correct.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, in particular, if we look behind tab 12, for example, Ramush Haradinaj authorises Tahir Zemaj to form a particular brigade?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Are you aware of a swearing-in ceremony that took place in Vranoc on the 20th of July in which Ramush Haradinaj and Tahir Zemaj jointly swore-in a large number of volunteers?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present there. I have also the medal at home. I was there with Ramush and Tahir. It's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the sake of the record, behind tab 18 is a transcript of a video of that swearing-in ceremony showing Mr. Haradinaj and Mr. Zemaj together. I don't propose to play the video because I will run out of my time if I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you like to have the transcript in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, if I may say so, it would be helpful to have that recorded in evidence and given an MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we do that now. The transcript of swearing-in, Madam Registrar, which is 1D14/0031 would receive what number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit D41 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I should, obviously, make it clear. And it's in the document, that this is the nature of a summary and a transcript. So it cross-refers to the video counter to indicate the activity that's taking place. And at some convenient moment, we would invite Your Honours to look at the video, which has a date counter on it, to see the swearing-in ceremony of the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would not like that to be played but you would like to have the video, as such, in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I don't propose to play it in this witness's evidence because I'll run out of time if I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, Madam Registrar, it's not just the transcript but it is the video as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to another collection of topics at this point. I'm entirely in Your Honours' hands when you would like to take the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we ask, if you have another subject, for five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But really five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I will stop you this document because we are very often talking about interpreters' duties, we are very often talking about technicians, but also transcribers, I would not like to have my fingers under such stress for such time, and security, et cetera. I will stop you if you have not finished by quarter to technical.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll stop slightly shy of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Two short questions, if I can. First of all, you were asked this morning about two different versions that you had heard about the death of two Serbs, one called Slobodan and one called Milos in Dashinoc or Dasinovac. And you told us in answer to Mr. Re that one of the accounts that you had heard had come to you directly from the person who was there, Deli Lekaj. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Deli Lekaj was injured. I went to visit him. He told me that -- I don't know which of them injured him. So there should not be any misunderstanding. He was injured, and then he told me what had happened. However, they were both alive when they did talk to me [as interpreted]. I don't know. There could be several versions about these two people. One version was they went to Prilep. They were released by Ramush. There was another version that they were in Dashinoc. So there were different variants. There were suppositions. I don't want to manipulate what happened. I cannot tell you that this one is true and this one is false. I also heard about Lahi Brahimaj, who burned [as interpreted] them, but this was only hearsay --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tetaj --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think "burned" may be a mistranslation or a mistranscription. I think the witness's evidence was "buried" rather than "burned."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they were not burnt. They were dead and then they were buried.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. At the same time, could you seek clarification, Mr. Emmerson, where he said: "However, they were both alive when they did talk to me."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: At that point, I think there is an error in the transcript I heard: "When Deli talked to me." And it came out as, "they did."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That was my understanding as well, but I can seek clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I put it to you this way, Mr. Tetaj, is it right that there were a lot of different rumours circulating, first of all?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you did manage to speak to one of the people who'd actually been involved in an exchange of fire with these two men, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. He was injured. He was injured by Slobodan,; and when I talked to Deli, Slobodan was alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Pause there. How do you know that Slobodan was alive when you spoke to Deli?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the doctor intervened, Syl Berisha, then people told me that they were free. They were seen on the way to Prilep.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. I see. Concentrating on the conversation with -- concentrating on the conversation with Deli Lekaj for a moment, did you see his injury?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you recognise it as a gun-shot wound?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the wound. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I think we may have got slightly out of sequence. Could you recognise the wound as a gun-shot wound?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me the -- he talked to me about the wound. The doctor also told me that it was a gun-shot wound, but I didn't see. That is what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. And later on, after the subzones were established at the end of May, Deli Lekaj became one of the officers who was under your immediate command, didn't he, in Lumbardh?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. We're just about to take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder to save time, if I might ask the witness, during the break, to cast his eye over some paragraphs in the document that appears at tab 20 so that we can save time over the break, if that's acceptable to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it, Mr. Re, that there's no objection against that. Tab 20, are you intending to tender that because it's not assigned a number yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I see how the witness's evidence emerges, and then make submissions on that once I hear his answers?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You found this, Mr. Tetaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: First, it is in English and then it is in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I said tab 10, and I should have said tab 20. That's the confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I think you said 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did I?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 20, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before my friend goes on, Mr. Emmerson goes on, there are some issues involved here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I asked whether there was any objection against the witness to read. I would expect Mr. Emmerson just to point at, not to summarize or in any other way, but just to say please read this and this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Paragraphs 7 to 10 is what I wanted to ask witness to look at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that be a problem for you, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Not if he expresses it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Tetaj, would you find during the break an opportunity to read in your own language paragraph 7 up to and including 10 so that Mr. Emmerson can ask questions about the matter after the break. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then let's break and resume at five minutes past.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before you leave the bench, can I raise something in the absence of the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do I take it with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you would be so kind as to read paragraphs 7 to 10 and Madam Usher will escort you out of the courtroom. Mr. Re, you would like to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, as far as the translation of P140 is concerned, your silence on the new translation introduced, I took that as consent to have the provisional translation also taken out of the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You read my silence correctly there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Given the concerns that were raised just before the break, I think I ought to conduct this part of my cross-examination in private session, provisionally, at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to ask you now one or two questions about another instance, in which you say that Ramush Haradinaj tried to intervene, and that is the case of Skender Kuci. First of all, you told us yesterday, I think, that when you came to tell Ramush Haradinaj that Skender Kuci had been detained, he knew nothing of it. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I discussed about this with Ramush. Ramush was very sad about such a gesture. He told me, "Wait a minute," and then we took a car. Together we went, as I described yesterday. I could confirm that for the first time he learned about this from me. This was the contact which actually gave to him information about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And your recollection is that on arrival and in conversation with Nazmi Brahimaj, Ramush Haradinaj tried to secure this man's immediate release by directing him to be released straight away. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you said that you continued to make inquiries about Skender Kuci, and that you learnt that he'd been taken to the hospital at Irzniq, is that correct, at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That person came. This happened later, after two or three days --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- he was not released. So they told me that he was not released, and I made inquiries together with Nazmi. We went to Jablanica. There we met with Nazmi Brahimaj. Nazmi was very desperate about this case. He expressed his condolences. He told us that there was an ambulance in the village of Irzniq to provide assistance; however, nothing could be done and he died. So he was taken back from the hospital to Irzniq, where he was buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There may be some confusion in the last answer that you've given. I want to clarify two words if I may. You say there was an ambulance in Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Are you referring -- just so we're clearer, are you referring to a makeshift field hospital?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, makeshift field hospital. It was not a hospital in the proper sense of the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But it wasn't a vehicle? The word "ambulance" in English means a moving vehicle. It wasn't a vehicle. It was a building?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. There were some nurses and some doctors in this place. It was a makeshift field hospital which was there and was operating under extraordinary circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: May I ask where was that hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In the village of Irzniq in Dodaj of that village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just to pick up another answer that I think may have been misunderstood at line 24, 25 on page 89, you say there that Nazmi told you that there was an ambulance; however, nothing could be done and he died. So he was taken back from the hospital to Irzniq where he was buried. Did you mean to say that he was taken to Irzniq, where he was buried, or that he was taken to Jablanica, where he was buried?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is so. When he was alive, he was sent to that hospital, where he died. And from the hospital, he was taken back to Jablanica, where he was buried. That is the sequence of events.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you now look behind tab 22 where we have the statement of doctor who treated him at the field hospital in Irzniq. We do not have this, I'm afraid to say, in Albanian. So I'm going to have to read to you the passage in English. It's behind tab 23. I'm noticing that we don't have an Albanian translation of that particular statement. So let me just read you the passage it's on paragraph 8. Just bear with me, I will read it to you slowly in English, and they will translate it to you so you can listen to it. This is a statement of Haki Shehu, who is a doctor at Irzniq hospital, specialising in internal injuries.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of Irzniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is about nine lines into paragraph 8: "Kuci was brought inside, and I made the first examination of his health conditions. I could not see any open wounds, and he was in a state of delirium. He was disoriented and not able to communicate. At the first look, he had symptoms of a person who had kidney problems because he had a swollen face, swollen feet, and swollen hands. Later on it was found that he had a kidney failure, and that both kidneys were completely blocked. Besides this I could recognise signs of cyanosis or bruises on his legs." I'll pause. "Signs of cyanosis are caused by injuries, heart dysfunction, beaten, or staying in conditions such as a cold or wet environment. The causes might vary but I don't know what it was in this specific case. The reason for the kidney failure of Kuci may have several reasons. Perhaps he had experienced a situation of shock. Maybe he suffered from low blood pressure or other illness. We did everything we could for him, but in fact he would have needed dialysis with CAPD which is a special liquid for these extreme kidney problems." I'll pause. "Unfortunately, we did not have this liquid. I did not see any other signs of injuries on his body. I can't evaluate the causes of his bruises, as we did not know at this point of time." Now, pausing there, there are two things I want to ask you. First of all, from the inquiries that you made, was it your understanding that he was still alive when he arrived at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The problems were related to his kidneys, and the hospital did not have the instruments and the means to cure it. This was confirmed to me by Nazmi. And I went there simply to find out if I could help, but there I was told that he had died and then I was starting to ask what had gone wrong. And what you read out was confirmed to me by Nazmi Brahimaj, and he was very sad about the whole thing. And they were just in front of a fact, and they had to act after that. Ramiz Berisha, who was there with me, said that we would like to unter him and re-bury him near his house, and Nazmi agreed to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there just because I'm working against the clock. Can you answer my next question yes or no. From the conversations you had with his family, did you become aware that Skender Kuci had a pre-existing kidney condition from a long time previously? Is that something that you found out or not?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never had such conversation with his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. That's helpful. Third question: Was it your understanding also that he had no wounds to his body; in other words, no open wounds on his body? Was that also your understanding?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that I knew was that when was untered, his corpse was untered, he was covered by soil, and I couldn't see any signs of open wounds. It was an overall bruising of the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In particular, Mr. Tetaj, there is a person, whose name I won't mention at this stage, who has made a witness statement --

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- claiming to have seen Skender Kuci with his kidney outside his bodies, having been ripped from inside and lying on the outside of his body. Now, I'm going to suggest to you that that is completely inconsistent, both with the medical report and with what you found out at the time.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not correct. That's not true. His body was one whole piece, but it was like black. It was a dark colour. I've seen it with my own eyes. It held all the pieces, and it was all in one piece. All the organs were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there I could see no kidney outside his body, and his family knows this; his wife, one of his closest loved ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand that, and it's not a member of his family that I'm referring to. It's someone quite different. Last couple of questions, if I may.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to ask you about a family who lived in Turjake, T-u-r-j-a-k-e.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Turjake.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You know the village of Turjake, and I want to ask you about a man called Istref Krasniqi. Pause for a moment, and I want to see if I can refresh your memory about Istref Krasniqi. Were you at one point in the summer of 1998, did you visit a family in Turjake who had become involved in a blood feud with another family in Turjake?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I have been to Turjake with the aim of expanding our operational zone so we could expand our operations; and in the village, there was several problems between the various quarters of the village. And I was there at the end of the village, where I saw a person who was immobile - that's what I've seen - and with wounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just pause there for a moment. We'll come back to the person.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the first name, but I knew that he was Krasniqi by family name.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In fact, is it right to say, in Turjake, there were two sets of blood feuds going on: One between two families who were both called Krasniqi, and one between a family of a man who was called Smajl Gashi and another family. And you were there trying to persuade these people to put their differences aside, is that right, in the interests of unity?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite right. That's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just to sketch in a little more of the detail, can you confirm that in the case of Istref Krasniqi, the blood feud had involved the situation where a few years earlier, Istref Krasniqi, his son Imer, and his daughter had all been sent to prison for murdering a man called Muharem Gjocaj because they thought that Muharem Gjocaj was going to try to elope with a member of their family. Does that accord with your recollection?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm anything about this. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I knew they had problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. In simple terms, then, let me put it this way: Were you aware that with the Krasniqi family, members of their family had killed members of the other Krasniqi family and revenge had been taken on them. There was a blood feud going on between the two Krasniqi families. Is that something you were aware of and trying to resolve?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a blood feud, yes, that's correct. But what was the basis for it, I did not have time to get into the detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Has anybody ever mentioned to you, anybody on the Prosecution team, for example, that it's alleged against you that you were responsible for the abduction of Istref Krasniqi, whose name is mentioned on this indictment? Has Mr. Re ever told you that or Ms. Gustafson that you are suggested to have been responsible for the abduction of Istref Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I only know from a book written by Tahir Zemaj, where it is said that I was accused of this. What I've done is I helped that family. I took flour to that family to help them, and there are numerous people in that village who testified to that. They were in serious -- in a serious blood feud, and there was nothing to stop them from killing each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't think there's any dispute that they were in a blood feud. I think the family themselves say so, but I want to ask you this: Has none of the Prosecution team ever asked you about this incident, or put to you that you were responsible for the disappearance of Istref and Nurije Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my first visit, I, myself, raised the issue because I wanted to clarify my position. I insisted; they didn't ask. But I insisted to clarify this because I read it in Tahir Zemaj's book. But recently, no, I haven't been asked or told.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was there any -- that's an answer I need to follow-up, because there's no mention in the written witness statement that you made in 2002 of this incident. So when you told the investigators about it in 2002, did they say anything to you about whether it should be recorded in your statement, what you were saying about Istref Krasniqi, or did they simply suggest to you that it should be left out?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not insist on such an element, as far as I remember. As far as I remember, it was very little discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Are you aware that one of the murders alleged on this indictment relates to those two individuals in Count 22? Were you aware of that before you came into court today? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: RRUSTEM TETAJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know. I don't know about this. No idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Those are my questions, Your Honour. I've concluded my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Emmerson. Mr. Tetaj, we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- could not finish today, so tomorrow we'll continue, also in the morning at 9.00, in this same courtroom. I, again, instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have given already or you're still about to give. Tomorrow you'll be cross-examined by counsel for the other defendants, and there may be more questions from the Bench or from Mr. Re. We stand adjourned until tomorrow, the 9th of May, 9.00, same courtroom.
